english: For what is the portion from God above, and the heritage from the Almighty on high?

paite: Midikloute tung ah siatna, gitlouh nasemte tung ah gawtna atung kei maw?
english: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous, and disaster to the workers of iniquity?

paite: Ama'n ka lampite amu kei a hia? ka kalsuante asim vek kei a hia?
english: Doesn’t he see my ways, and number all my steps?

paite: "Thuzuau toh na om a, huai a ka khe khem ding a kinoh ahihleh;
english: “If I have walked with falsehood, and my foot has hurried to deceit

paite: bukna diktak ah hon buk dih ua, Pathian in ka thutakna thei hen!
english: (let me be weighed in an even balance, that God may know my integrity);

paite: Ka kalsuan lampi a kipan a na pial hiam, ka lungtang in ka mitte na zui hiam, ka khutte ah nin himhim na belh hiam;
english: if my step has turned out of the way, if my heart walked after my eyes, if any defilement has stuck to my hands,

paite: Huchi ka hihleh, chi tuh ning, midang in ne hen; ahi, ka lou a piang bulkalh khiak hi hen.
english: then let me sow, and let another eat. Yes, let the produce of my field be rooted out.

paite: "Ka lungtang numei lam a khem a om a, ka inveng kongkhak ka na ngak takleh;
english: “If my heart has been enticed to a woman, and I have laid wait at my neighbor’s door,

paite: huchi ahih takleh ka zi in midang a ding in an su henla, midangte amah tung ah kun uhen.
english: then let my wife grind for another, and let others sleep with her.

paite: Huchibang gitlouhna hoih het lou ahi; ahi, vaihawm mite gawt ding khelhna ngei,
english: For that would be a heinous crime. Yes, it would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges:

paite: siatna ding a Abaddon tan a kangbei leh, ka punna tengteng zungkalh ding mei hi ding lah ahi ngal a.
english: For it is a fire that consumes to destruction, and would root out all my increase.

paite: "Ka tung a phunna aneih lai ua, ka sikhapa hiam ka sikhanu hiam makhua na musit a, na khualsak lou ka hihleh;
english: “If I have despised the cause of my male servant or of my female servant, when they contended with me;

paite: Pathian athohkhiak chiang in bang ka hihta dia? Thu akan hun chiang in bang in ka dawngta dia?
english: What then shall I do when God rises up? When he visits, what shall I answer him?

paite: Kei sul a pan hon bawlpa'n amah abawl kei maw? Khat in ahon bawl tuak ahi kei maw?
english: Didn’t he who made me in the womb make him? Didn’t one fashion us in the womb?

paite: "Migentheite alunggulh uh ka piak louh a, ahihkeileh vuaksuak ding a meithai mitte ka na omsakleh;
english: “If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,

paite: Ahihkeileh kei kia in ka an ka nek a, huai a pabei in an anek keileh;
english: or have eaten my morsel alone, and the fatherless has not eaten of it

paite: Ii, ka tuailai a kipan in pa bang ka hi, ka kiang ah ana khanglianta; ka nu sul a kipan amah pipa ka hita hi.
english: (no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, her have I guided from my mother’s womb);

paite: "Kuapeuh taksap ziak a mangthang hiam, ahihkeileh tasam khuhna nei lou hiam ka na muhleh;
english: if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering;

paite: Akawngte'n kei hon vualzawl lou a, ka belam mul a lumsak a ana om keileh.
english: if his heart hasn’t blessed me, if he hasn’t been warmed with my sheep’s fleece;

paite: "Kongpi a panpihna ka muh ziak a pabeite siatna ding a ka khut ka na likleh;
english: if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless, because I saw my help in the gate,

paite: Huchi ka hihleh, ka liang ka liangzang a kipan kia henla, aguh a kipan ka ban kitan hen.
english: then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder blade, and my arm be broken from the bone.

paite: Pathian a kipan tuahsia kei a ding in launa ahi ngal a, athupina ka tuak ngam kei hi.
english: For calamity from God is a terror to me. Because his majesty, I can do nothing.

paite: "Dangka-eng lametpen a ka na bawl a, dangka-eng hoih kiang ah, ka muanna na hi, ka na chihtak a;
english: “If I have made gold my hope, and have said to the fine gold, ‘You are my confidence;’

paite: Ka hauhna thupi ziak a hiam, ka khut in tam alam ziak a ka kipah a;
english: If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, and because my hand had gotten much;

paite: Avak lai a ni ka na et a, kha thupitak paikhia ka na et a,
english: if I have seen the sun when it shined, or the moon moving in splendor,

paite: Ka lungtang guk a khem a a-om a, ka kam in ka khut ana tawp takleh;
english: and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my hand threw a kiss from my mouth,

paite: Hiai leng thulimlouhna vaihawmte gawt ding ahi, tung a Pathian kiang a na zuauta hi ding ka hih ziak in.
english: this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges; for I should have denied the God who is above.

paite: "Kei hon mudah siatna a ka na kipah a, ahihkeileh hoih lou atung a atun chiang a ka na kipah luatleh;
english: “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him;

paite: Ka melma hamsiat ding leh ahenna thum ding in ka kam ka na khialsak kei.
english: (yes, I have not allowed my mouth to sin by asking his life with a curse);

paite: Ka puaninte a, 'A-an a kihihvah lou kua a-om a?' hon na chih kei ualeh;
english: if the men of my tent have not said, ‘Who can find one who has not been filled with his meat?’

paite: Kongzing ah mikhual agiak ngei kei a; khualzin a ding in ka kongte ka na hongta.
english: (the foreigner has not lodged in the street, but I have opened my doors to the traveler);

paite: "Adam bang a ka angsung a thulimlouhna na sel a, ka tatlekna na khuh ka hih a,
english: if like Adam I have covered my transgressions, by hiding my iniquity in my heart,

paite: aziak, mi tampi launa thupitak ka neih ziak ahih a, sungte hon muh daina launa ziak a huchi a dai dide a, popawt lou ka hihleh,
english: because I feared the great multitude, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I kept silence, and didn’t go out of the door—

paite: Aw, kei hon za ding mi nei leng maw. Ngai in, ka deihlam hiai ahi. Bangkim hihthei in hon dawng henla; ka melma in laibu ah gelhkhiak hen.
english: oh that I had one to hear me! (behold, here is my signature, let the Almighty answer me); let the accuser write my indictment!

paite: "Chihtaktak in ka liangzang ah ka po dia; lallukhu bang in kei ah ka kan den ding hi.
english: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; and I would bind it to me as a crown.

paite: Akiang ah ka kalsuan zah ka puang ding a; lal bang in akiangnai ah ka hoh ding hi.
english: I would declare to him the number of my steps. as a prince would I go near to him.

paite: "Ka gam kei dem a akikou a, lei lehsate akahkhawm uleh;
english: If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep together;

paite: Sum lou a huai gahte ka na nek tak a, ahihkeileh huai a aneite ahinna uh ka na tansakleh,
english: if I have eaten its fruits without money, or have caused its owners to lose their life,

paite: Buh hilou in louling neite, barli buh hilou in loubualte pou zaw hen," Job thute abeita hi.
english: let briars grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley.” The words of Job are ended.

paite: Huchibang in hiai mi thumte Job dawn atawpta ua, amah mit a diktat ahih ziak in.
english: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

paite: Huai lai in Job tung ah Ram inkuan a Buz mi Barakel tapa Elihu hehna akuangkhia a, Pathian hi zaw lou a amah siam akitansak ziak in.
english: Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel, the Buzite, of the family of Ram, was kindled against Job. His wrath was kindled because he justified himself rather than God.

paite: Alawm thumte tung ah leng ahehna akuangkhia a, dawnna ding nei lou a, hinapi a lah Job amohpaih ziak un.
english: Also his wrath was kindled against his three friends, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.

paite: Amah sang a a-upat zawk ziak un, Job kiang a thu gen ding in Elihu in angak hi.
english: Now Elihu had waited to speak to Job, because they were elder than he.

paite: Hiai mi thumte kam a dawnna a-om kei chih atheih in, ahehna akuangkhia hi.
english: When Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, his wrath was kindled.

paite: "Huchi in Buz mi Barakel tapa. Elihu in adawng hi: Ka naupang a, noute na upa mahmah uh; huaiziak in ka dai a, ka lungsim ka hon ensak ngam kei hi.
english: Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite answered, “I am young, and you are very old; Therefore I held back, and didn’t dare show you my opinion.

paite: Huchi in ka chi, 'Nite'n thu agen ding uh, kum tampi in pilna a sinsak ding hi.'
english: I said, ‘Days should speak, and multitude of years should teach wisdom.’

paite: Himahleh mihing lungsim a om a, Bangkim hihthei in theihsiamna apia hi.
english: But there is a spirit in man, and the breath of the Almighty gives them understanding.

paite: Apilte mithupite ahi kei ua, vaihawmna theisiamte upate ahi sam kei uh.
english: It is not the great who are wise, nor the aged who understand justice.

paite: Huaiziak in hong ngaikhia un; ke'n leng ka lungsim ka ensak ding, ka chi.
english: Therefore I said, ‘Listen to me; I also will show my opinion.’

paite: "Ngai un, na thute uh ka ngak a, gen ding na zonkhiak lai un, na thusutte uh ka ngaikhia.
english: “Behold, I waited for your words, and I listened for your reasoning, while you searched out what to say.

paite: Ahi, ka hon limsak a, ngai un, kuamah Job thuzoh zou na om kei uh, ahihkeileh na lak uah, athute dawng.
english: Yes, I gave you my full attention, but there was no one who convinced Job, or who answered his words, among you.

paite: Pilna i muta, chi lou ding in pilvang un; mihing hilou in Pathian in amah azou thei hi.
english: Beware lest you say, ‘We have found wisdom, God may refute him, not man;’

paite: Ama'n kei siatna ding in athute ahih kei a; ke'n leng nou thugente in amah ka dawng sam kei ding.
english: for he has not directed his words against me; neither will I answer him with your speeches.

paite: "Lamdang sa in, adawng nawn akei ua, gen ding thu khat leng anei kei uh.
english: “They are amazed. They answer no more. They don’t have a word to say.

paite: Thu ging neih louh ziak in adingh kinken ua, adawn nawn louh ziak un ke'n ka ngak diam?
english: Shall I wait, because they don’t speak, because they stand still, and answer no more?

paite: Ke'n leng ka dawnna ding ka nei hi, ka lungsim ka ensak sam ding, ka chi hi.
english: I also will answer my part, and I also will show my opinion.

paite: Thu in ka dim a; ka sung a ka kha in hon sawl teitei hi.
english: For I am full of words. The spirit within me constrains me.

paite: Ngai un, ka gilpi pawtkhiakna nei lou uain thawl bang ahi; uain thawl thakte bang in puakzak ding in mansa in ma-om hi.
english: Behold, my breast is as wine which has no vent; like new wineskins it is ready to burst.

paite: Ka halhtheihna ding in, ka pau ding; ka mukte ka hong dia, ka dawng ding hi.
english: I will speak, that I may be refreshed. I will open my lips and answer.

paite: Mihing mihinna zahtaksak kei un, ka hon ngen hi; kuamah kiang ah leng maitang phatna min ka pe kei ding hi.
english: Please don’t let me respect any man’s person, neither will I give flattering titles to any man.

paite: Maitang phatna minte piak ding ka thei ngal kei a; huchi lou in zaw kei hon bawlpa'n ahon lazok ding hi."
english: For I don’t know how to give flattering titles; or else my Maker would soon take me away.

paite: "Akoi abang hitaleh, Job, ka hon ngen hi, thugen za inla ka thugen tengteng ngaikhia in.
english: “However, Job, please hear my speech, and listen to all my words.

paite: Ngai in, tu in, ka kam ka ka a, ka kam in ka pau hi.
english: See now, I have opened my mouth. My tongue has spoken in my mouth.

paite: Ka thute'n ka lungtang dikna agenkhe ding uh; Ka mukte'n atheih ngei uh chihtaktak in agen ding uhi.
english: My words shall utter the uprightness of my heart. That which my lips know they shall speak sincerely.

paite: Pathian Kha in ahon bawl a, Bangkim hihthei hu in hinna ahon pia hi.
english: The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.

paite: "Na theihleh hon dawng in; ka ma ah na thute akizom in koih inla na panna ah dingh in.
english: If you can, answer me. Set your words in order before me, and stand forth.

paite: Ngai in, nang bang in Pathian lam ah ka om hi; kei leng tungman a bawl ka hi.
english: Behold, I am toward God even as you are. I am also formed out of the clay.

paite: Ngai in, ka lauhuaina in nang ahon lausak kei ding, ka hahkatna leng na tung ah agik kei ding hi.
english: Behold, my terror shall not make you afraid, neither shall my pressure be heavy on you.

paite: "Chihtaktak in ka zak in na pauta a, huchi in na thute ging ka zata hi.
english: “Surely you have spoken in my hearing, I have heard the voice of your words, saying,

paite: Ka siang hi, tatlekna bei; ka hoih a, kei ah thulimlouhna leng a-om kei, chi in.
english: ‘I am clean, without disobedience. I am innocent, neither is there iniquity in me.

paite: Ngai in, kei demna ding ziak amu a melma in ahon simta hi;
english: Behold, he finds occasions against me. He counts me for his enemy.

paite: Ka khete kol abunsak a, ka lampite tengteng achiamteh hi.
english: He puts my feet in the stocks. He marks all my paths.’

paite: "Ngai in, ka hon dawng ding, hiai na diklouhna ah; mihing sang in Pathian alianzaw hi.
english: “Behold, I will answer you. In this you are not just, for God is greater than man.

paite: Bangziak a amah dou na hia, Ka thute a bangmah mah lah adawng kei ding, chi in?
english: Why do you strive against him, because he doesn’t give account of any of his matters?

paite: Pathian in lah khatvei agen a, ahi, nihvei, mihing in limsak kei mahleh.
english: For God speaks once, yes twice, though man pays no attention.

paite: Zan a mang ah, mengmuhna ah, mite tung a ihmut kip akiak lai un, lupna tung a ihmut laite un;
english: In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on men, in slumbering on the bed;

paite: huai lai in mite bilte ahong a, vaunate in amau ahihlau a,
english: Then he opens the ears of men, and seals their instruction,

paite: Huchi a athiltup a kipan a mihing alakkika, mihing a kipan akisaktheihna asatkhiak theihna ding in;
english: That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.

paite: Ama'n kokhuk a kipan akha akepkiksak a, namsau a kipan ahinna.
english: He keeps back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword.

paite: "Alupna tung ah natna asawi in leng a-om aguhte akinakna om gige toh in.
english: He is chastened also with pain on his bed, with continual strife in his bones;

paite: Huchi in ahinna in tanghou, akha in an lim akih hi.
english: So that his life abhors bread, and his soul dainty food.

paite: Asa atummang a, huchi in muh theih in a-om kei; Akimu lou a guhte hong dawkkhia uhi.
english: His flesh is so consumed away, that it can’t be seen. His bones that were not seen stick out.

paite: Ahi, han kiang ah akha ahong nai a, ahinna hihse mite kiang ah.
english: Yes, his soul draws near to the pit, and his life to the destroyers.

paite: "Akiang a angel, kamlet, sangkhat lak a khat, mihing kiang a amah a dia dik bang ahia chih etsak ding a-omleh;
english: “If there is beside him an angel, an interpreter, one among a thousand, to show to man what is right for him;

paite: Huchi a amah a ding a zahngai thei, Kokhuk a paisukna a kipan amah suaktasak un, tatna ka muta.
english: then God is gracious to him, and says, ‘Deliver him from going down to the pit, I have found a ransom.’

paite: Asa naupang a sang in nou zaw hen; atuailai nite lam ah kik nawnta hen.
english: His flesh shall be fresher than a child’s. He returns to the days of his youth.

paite: Pathian kiang ah athum a, amah ding in deihsak theih in a-om hi; huchi in nopna toh amai amu a; adiktatna akiang ah ape nawn hi.
english: He prays to God, and he is favorable to him, so that he sees his face with joy. He restores to man his righteousness.

paite: Mite ma ah la asa a, ka khialta a, adik ka na hekkawi a, thuk in ka om kei!
english: He sings before men, and says, ‘I have sinned, and perverted that which was right, and it didn’t profit me.

paite: Kokhuk sung a paisukna a kipan akha atanta hi, ahinna in vakna amuta ding hi, achi a.
english: He has redeemed my soul from going into the pit. My life shall see the light.’

paite: "Ngai in, hiai thilte tengteng Pathian in, mihing lak ah ahih a, nihvei, ahi thumvei.
english: “Behold, God works all these things, twice, yes three times, with a man,

paite: Kokhuk a kipan akha pikik ding in, huchi a mihing vakna ahihvak a a-omtheihna ding in.
english: to bring back his soul from the pit, that he may be enlightened with the light of the living.

paite: "Chiamteh in, Aw Job, ngaikhia in, dai inla, thu ka gen ding.
english: Mark well, Job, and listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will speak.

paite: Gen ding na neihleh, hon dawng in, pau in, siam hon tansak ka ut ngal a.
english: If you have anything to say, answer me. Speak, for I desire to justify you.

paite: Na neih keileh, kei hon ngaikhia in, dai inla pilna ka hon sinsak ding hi."
english: If not, listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom.”

paite: Huai lou in Elihu in adawng a, hichi in achi:
"Ka thute za un, nou mipilte; nou theihna neite, bil hon doh un.
english: “Hear my words, you wise men. Give ear to me, you who have knowledge.

paite: Dangtawng in an achep bang in, bil in thute a-enchian hi.
english: For the ear tries words, as the palate tastes food.

paite: Adik ei a ding in i tel ding uh; i lak ua hoih bang ahia i thei ding uh.
english: Let us choose for us that which is right. Let us know among ourselves what is good.

paite: Job in, 'Ka dik a, Pathian in ka dikna a lamang,' achi ngal a.
english: For Job has said, ‘I am righteous, God has taken away my right:

paite: Ka dikna huchi hita mahleh zuauthei a sim ka hi a; tatlekna bei himah leng, ka liamna hihdam theih louh ahi.
english: Notwithstanding my right I am considered a liar. My wound is incurable, though I am without disobedience.’

paite: "Muhsitna tui bang a dawn bei, Job bang mihing kua ahia?
english: What man is like Job, who drinks scorn like water,

paite: Thulim lou nasem mite toh ahon a pai, migiloute toh omkhawm mi.
english: Who goes in company with the workers of iniquity, and walks with wicked men?

paite: Ama'n lah, 'Pathian lak a ka kipahna ding bangmah ka loh tak kei,' achi ngal a.
english: For he has said, ‘It profits a man nothing that he should delight himself with God.’

paite: Huaiziak in nou theisiam mite, hon ngaikhia un. Pathian in, gilou bangchi in ahih ngei dia; Bangkim hihthei in thulim lou bangchi in ahih mahmah dia.
english: “Therefore listen to me, you men of understanding: far be it from God, that he should do wickedness, from the Almighty, that he should commit iniquity.

paite: Ama'n lah mihing thilhih amah kiang apekik ding a, mi chiteng alampite kiang a pekik ding ahi.
english: For the work of a man he will render to him, and cause every man to find according to his ways.

paite: "Ahi, moh khuksakna thu ah, Pathian in giloutak in ahih kei dia, Bangkim hihthei in leng vaihawmna ahihse sam kei ding hi.
english: Yes surely, God will not do wickedly, neither will the Almighty pervert justice.

paite: Kua'n ahia amah leitung heutu hihna pia? Ahihkeileh khovel pumpi kua'n ahia athu a koih?
english: Who put him in charge of the earth? or who has appointed him over the whole world?

paite: Mihing tung a alungtang nga a, ama lam a akha leh ahu lakhawm;
english: If he set his heart on himself, If he gathered to himself his spirit and his breath,

paite: Sa tengteng amangthang vek ding ua, mihing leivui asuak nawn ding hi.
english: all flesh would perish together, and man would turn again to dust.

paite: "Theihsiamna na neihleh, hiai za in; ka thu aw ngaikhia in.
english: “If now you have understanding, hear this. Listen to the voice of my words.

paite: Mi thudik hua in vai ahawm ding hia? Dik leh hat amah na mohpaih ding hia?
english: Shall even one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn him who is righteous and mighty?—

paite: Kumpipa kiang a, 'Na hoih kei' chih akilawm hia? Ahihkeileh miliante kiang a, 'Na gilou uh?' chih.
english: Who says to a king, ‘Vile!’ or to nobles, ‘Wicked!’?

paite: Milalte mihinna zahtak lou a, Genthei sang a mihausate limsak zawte kiang a chih akilawm sem lou ding hia? Amaute lah akhut nasep ahi ngal ua.
english: Who doesn’t respect the persons of princes, nor respects the rich more than the poor; for they all are the work of his hands.

paite: Mitphiat kal lou in asi ua zankim lai mahmah in; mite aling ua apaimang ua, mihing khut hilou in mihatte lakmang in a-om uhi.
english: In a moment they die, even at midnight. The people are shaken and pass away. The mighty are taken away without a hand.

paite: "Amitte mihing lampite tung ah a-om a, apainate amu hi.
english: “For his eyes are on the ways of a man. He sees all his goings.

paite: Thulim lou nasem mite bukna ding khomial hiam limliap hiam a-om kei hi.
english: There is no darkness, nor thick gloom, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves.

paite: Vaihawmna a Pathian ma a pai ding in, mihing angaihtuah lailai akiphamoh kei hi.
english: For he doesn’t need to consider a man further, that he should go before God in judgment.

paite: Lamte theih phak vual louh in ama'n mihatte ahihzan vek a, amun uah midang atungkhia hi.
english: He breaks in pieces mighty men in ways past finding out, and sets others in their place.

paite: Huaiziak in anasepte uh athei hi; zan in amau alumlet a, hihsiat in a-om uhi.
english: Therefore he takes knowledge of their works. He overturns them in the night, so that they are destroyed.

paite: Midang mitmuh mahmah in migiloute bang in amau agawt hi.
english: He strikes them as wicked men in the open sight of others;

paite: Amah zuihna a kipan apialkhiak ua, alampite a koimah alimsak louh ziak un.
english: because they turned aside from following him, and wouldn’t pay attention to any of his ways,

paite: Huchi in mizawng kahna akiang tung ding in abawl ua, gimthuak kahna aza hi.
english: so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to him. He heard the cry of the afflicted.

paite: "Amah na pau keileh, kua'n siam louh atangsak dia? Ama'n amai aselleh, kua'n amah amu thei dia? Namte kiang a hih hiam, ahihkeileh mihing kiang a hih hiam akibang hi.
english: When he gives quietness, who then can condemn? When he hides his face, who then can see him? Alike whether to a nation, or to a man,

paite: Huchi a Pathian theiloumi in vai ahawm louh a, amite thang a awksak ding a- omlouhna ding in.
english: that the godless man may not reign, that there be no one to ensnare the people.

paite: "Kuapeuh in Pathian kiang ah, Gawtna ka thuakta, ka gilou nawn kei ding,
english: “For has any said to God, ‘I am guilty, but I will not offend any more.

paite: Ka muh louh nang hon sinsak in, gilou ka hihleh ka hih nawn kei ding, achi uhia?
english: Teach me that which I don’t see. If I have done iniquity, I will do it no more’?

paite: Athukna huchi a na nial na deih bang in a-om diam? Kei hilou in, nang na tel ngeingei ding ahi.
english: Shall his recompense be as you desire, that you refuse it? For you must choose, and not I. Therefore speak what you know.

paite: "Theisiam mite'n ka kiang ah, 'Ahi,' achi ding uh, aza mipil teng in.
english: Men of understanding will tell me, yes, every wise man who hears me:

paite: Job in theihna bei in thu agen a, athute pilna bei ahi uh.
english: ‘Job speaks without knowledge. His words are without wisdom.’

paite: Mihaite bang a adawnna ah, atawp chiang in Job tungtang ngaihtuah le uh.
english: I wish that Job were tried to the end, because of his answering like wicked men.

paite: Ama'n akhelhna ah helna abehlap a, i lak uah akhut abeng a, Pathian kalh in athu apungsakta hi.”
english: For he adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against God.”

paite: Elihu in adawng a, hichi in achi:
"Hiai na dikna hi in na ngaihtuah hia, ahihkeileh, kei a mawng ahi, Pathian mai ah na chi hia?
english: “Do you think this to be your right, or do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’

paite: Kei a ding in bang phattuamna a-om dia? Khial lou a ka om in bang phattuamna ka nei a? na chih.
english: That you ask, ‘What advantage will it be to you? What profit shall I have, more than if I had sinned?’

paite: Nang leh na kiang a na lawmte ka hon dawng ding.
english: I will answer you, and your companions with you.

paite: "Vante lam en inla, mu in; vante, nang sang a sangzaw, en in.
english: Look to the heavens, and see. See the skies, which are higher than you.

paite: Na hihkhelhleh, amah dem a bang hih na hia? Na tatleknate punsak hileh, amah tung a bang hih na hia?
english: If you have sinned, what effect do you have against him? If your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to him?

paite: Diktat na hihleh, amah bang na pia a? Ahihkeileh na khut a kipan bang amu a?
english: If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?

paite: Na gitlouhna in nang bang in mi ahihna thei a; na diktatna in mihing tapa ahih hampha thei hi.
english: Your wickedness may hurt a man as you are, and your righteousness may profit a son of man.

paite: Nuaisiahna atam mahmah ziak in akikoukhia ua; mihat ban ziak in panpih deih in akikou uh.
english: “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out. They cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty.

paite: Kuamah in, 'Zan chia late hon pia, Pathian kei hon Bawlpa koi a om ahia;
english: But none says, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,

paite: Lei a gamsate sang a hon sinsak tamzaw leh, van a vasate sang a hon pilsakzaw?' achi kei uh.
english: who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?’

paite: Huai ah akikou ua, himahleh, migilou kisaktheihna ziak in, kuamah in dawnna ape kei.
english: There they cry, but none gives answer, because of the pride of evil men.

paite: Chihtaktak in Pathian in bangmah lou aza kei dia, Bangkim hihthei in leng alimsaksak kei ding hi.
english: Surely God will not hear an empty cry, neither will the Almighty regard it.

paite: "Nang ngial in houh, ‘Amah ka mu kei, athu ma ah a-om, Amah ka ngak hi,' na chih vial.
english: How much less when you say you don’t see him. The cause is before him, and you wait for him!

paite: Himahleh tu in, heh a aveh louh a, ki-otsakna leng alimsak louh ziak in;
english: But now, because he has not visited in his anger, neither does he greatly regard arrogance.

paite: Huaiziak in Job in bangmah lou in akam aka ahi; theihna bei in thu atamsak ahi.”
english: Therefore Job opens his mouth with empty talk, and he multiplies words without knowledge.”

paite: Elihu mah in agenzom zel a, hichi in achi:
"Hon na thuakzou zek inla, huan ka hon ensak ding; Pathian sik in lah banghiam khat gen ding ka nei ngal a.
english: “Bear with me a little, and I will show you; for I still have something to say on God’s behalf.

paite: Gamla a kipan ka theihna ka hon la ding a, kei hon Bawlpa tung ah diktatna ka nga ding hi.
english: I will get my knowledge from afar, and will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.

paite: Diktak in ka thute zuau ahi kei a; hoihkim khat ka kiang ah a-om hi.
english: For truly my words are not false. One who is perfect in knowledge is with you.

paite: "Ngai in, Pathian in thil ahihthei a, kuamah amusit kei; theihsiamna hatna ah thil ahihthei hi.
english: “Behold, God is mighty, and doesn’t despise anyone. He is mighty in strength of understanding.

paite: Gilou hinna ahawi kei a; himahleh gimthuakte kiang ah adikna uh apia hi.
english: He doesn’t preserve the life of the wicked, but gives to the afflicted their right.

paite: Midiktat a kipan amit alakik kei; himahleh laltutphah tung a kumpipa toh amau tangtawn in akoih a, huchi in hihlet in a-om uhi.
english: He doesn’t withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but with kings on the throne, he sets them forever, and they are exalted.

paite: Huan sikkhaute a gak a a-om ua, gimthuakna guite alak a a-om uleh;
english: If they are bound in fetters, and are taken in the cords of afflictions,

paite: Huchi in athilhih uh amau a- ensak a, atatlekna uh, huchi a kisatheitak a ana omna uh.
english: then he shows them their work, and their transgressions, that they have behaved themselves proudly.

paite: Thuhilhna lam ah abil uh ahonsak a, thulimlouhna a kipan kik ding in thu apia hi.
english: He also opens their ears to instruction, and commands that they return from iniquity.

paite: Amah thu angaihkhiak ua, a-nna asep uh leh, anite uh hauhsakna in ahihbei ding ua, akumte uh kipahna in.
english: If they listen and serve him, they shall spend their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasures.

paite: Himahleh angaihkhiak kei ualeh, namsau in amangthang ding ua, huchi in theihna bei in asi ding uh.
english: But if they don’t listen, they shall perish by the sword; they shall die without knowledge.

paite: "Himahleh amau lungtang a Pathian limsaklouhnate'n hehna akholkhawm hi; amau ahen lai in panpih deih in akikou kei uh.
english: “But those who are godless in heart lay up anger. They don’t cry for help when he binds them.

paite: Tuailai in asi ua, siangloute lak ah ahinna uh amangthang hi.
english: They die in youth. Their life perishes among the unclean.

paite: Agimthuakna in gimthuakte asuaktasak a, nuaisiahna ah abil uh ahonsak hi.
english: He delivers the afflicted by their affliction, and opens their ear in oppression.

paite: Ahi, gakchihna omlouhna, mun lian lam ah dahna a kipan nang ahon pimang ding a; na dohkan tung a kilui thauna in adimta ding hi.
english: Yes, he would have allured you out of distress, into a broad place, where there is no restriction. That which is set on your table would be full of fatness.

paite: Himahleh giloute vaihawmna in na dim a; vaihawmna leh diktatna in nang hon len hi.
english: “But you are full of the judgment of the wicked. Judgment and justice take hold of you.

paite: Thangpaihna a-om ziak in, pilvang in huchi lou in zaw na hauhna in nang ahon pimang kha ding hi; golhgukna tampi in leng nang hon pialsak kei hen.
english: Don’t let riches entice you to wrath, neither let the great size of a bribe turn you aside.

paite: Dahna ana omlouhna ding in, na hauhsaknate ahun diam, ahihkeileh na hatna thilhihtheihna tengteng?
english: Would your wealth sustain you in distress, or all the might of your strength?

paite: Mite tengteng amun ua satkhiak a a-om zan uah lunggulh ke'n.
english: Don’t desire the night, when people are cut off in their place.

paite: Pilvang in, gilou limsak ke'n; gimthuakna sang in hiai lah na telzawta ngal a.
english: Take heed, don’t regard iniquity; for you have chosen this rather than affliction.

paite: "Ngai in, Pathian in athilhihtheihna in sangtak in ahih; amah bang sinsakmi kua ahia?
english: Behold, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?

paite: Kua'n amah alampi thu apia a? Ahihkeileh, 'Diklouhna na bawlta,' kua'n achi thei dia?
english: Who has prescribed his way for him? Or who can say, ‘You have committed unrighteousness?’

paite: Mite'n la asak uh, athilhih hihlian ding in theigige in.
english: “Remember that you magnify his work, whereof men have sung.

paite: Huai ah mite tengteng a-en ua; huai mihing in gamlapi ah amu hi.
english: All men have looked thereon. Man sees it afar off.

paite: Ngai in, Pathian alian a, amah i thei kei; akumte zah zontheih ahi kei.
english: Behold, God is great, and we don’t know him. The number of his years is unsearchable.

paite: "Tui takte ama'n atawi khin a, huai a tuihu a kipan vuah azu.
english: For he draws up the drops of water, which distill in rain from his vapor,

paite: Huai vante'n asungkhia ua, mihing tung ah tampi in atak.
english: Which the skies pour down and which drop on man abundantly.

paite: Meipi kiphahte leh a-inn vanpi gingte kua'n atheisiam dia?
english: Yes, can any understand the spreading of the clouds, and the thunderings of his pavilion?

paite: Ngai in, akim ah akhovak azak a; tuipi nuai atuam hi.
english: Behold, he spreads his light around him. He covers the bottom of the sea.

paite: Hiaite in mite avai hawmsak a; an tampi apia hi.
english: For by these he judges the people. He gives food in abundance.

paite: Akhutte in khophia atawi a; chiamtehna khoh ding in thu apia hi.
english: He covers his hands with the lightning, and commands it to strike the mark.

paite: Huai husa in atungtang thu agen a, ganhonte'n leng hong kuantou huihpi tungtang thu athei uh."
english: Its noise tells about him, and the livestock also concerning the storm that comes up.

paite: "Hiai ah leng ka lungtang aling a, amun a kipan suan in a-om hi.
english: “Yes, at this my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place.

paite: A-aw ging leh akam a kipan avan-ging paikhia noute'n ngaikhia un.
english: Hear, oh, hear the noise of his voice, the sound that goes out of his mouth.

paite: Van pumpi nuai ah asawlkhia a, akhophia lei tawpnate tan in.
english: He sends it forth under the whole sky, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.

paite: Huai zoh in aw akikou a; alalna aw in vanpi agingsak a: a-aw zak a a-om chiang in amau alen kei hi.
english: After it a voice roars. He thunders with the voice of his majesty. He doesn’t hold back anything when his voice is heard.

paite: Pathian in a-aw in lamdangtak in vanpi agingsak a; i theihtheih louh, thil thupite ahih zel hi.
english: God thunders marvelously with his voice. He does great things, which we can’t comprehend.

paite: Ama'n lah vuk kiang ah, 'Lei ah kia in,' achi ngal a; huchi mah bang in vuahmal phin kiang ah leng.
english: For he says to the snow, ‘Fall on the earth;’ likewise to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.

paite: Mi chiteng khut atuambit a; abawlsa mite tengteng in huai atheihtheihna ding un.
english: He seals up the hand of every man, that all men whom he has made may know it.

paite: Huai lai in gamsate amun uah alut ua, akuate uah a-om uhi.
english: Then the animals take cover, and remain in their dens.

paite: Simlam dantan a kipan huihpi ahong a; mallam a kipan khovot.
english: Out of its room comes the storm, and cold out of the north.

paite: Pathian hu in tui khal piak ahi; tuite nakna hihhaksat in a-om.
english: By the breath of God, ice is given, and the breadth of the waters is frozen.

paite: Ahi, meipi nawnna aposak a; akhophia meipi aphalhsak hi.
english: Yes, he loads the thick cloud with moisture. He spreads abroad the cloud of his lightning.

paite: Amah pi in akivial heihei ua, tentheihna khovel maikaih a amaute thu apiak peuhmah ahihna ding un.
english: It is turned around by his guidance, that they may do whatever he commands them on the surface of the habitable world,

paite: Bawlhoihna ding hiam, agam a ding hiam, ahihkeileh zahngaihna ding thiam a, ahon paisakna ah.
english: Whether it is for correction, or for his land, or for loving kindness, that he causes it to come.

paite: "Hiai ngaikhia in, Aw Job; dingh kinken inla, Pathian thilhih lamdangte ngaihtuah in.
english: “Listen to this, Job. Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God.

paite: Amaute tung a Pathian thupiak akoih a, ameipi khophia atansakdan na thei hia?
english: Do you know how God controls them, and causes the lightning of his cloud to shine?

paite: Meipite kibuk diknate, amah theihna hoihkim thilhih lamdangte na thei hia?
english: Do you know the workings of the clouds, the wondrous works of him who is perfect in knowledge?

paite: Sim huih ziak a lei adaih sipsip lai a, na puansilhte alumdan?
english: You whose clothing is warm, when the earth is still by reason of the south wind?

paite: Amah toh van, suntawm limlang bang a khauh na phalh thei hia?
english: Can you, with him, spread out the sky, which is strong as a cast metal mirror?

paite: Akiang a ka gen ding uh hon sinsak in; mialna ziak in ka thugen ding uh ka gelkhol thei kei ua.
english: Teach us what we shall tell him, for we can’t make our case by reason of darkness.

paite: Thu ka gen ding chih amah hilh ding ahi diam? Ahihkeileh mihing in valh khit a om ut ding ahi diam?
english: Shall it be told him that I would speak? Or should a man wish that he were swallowed up?

paite: "Huchi in mite'n meipi a om khovak amu kei ua: himahleh huih anung a, amaute ahihsiang hi.
english: Now men don’t see the light which is bright in the skies, but the wind passes, and clears them.

paite: Mal a kipan in dangka-eng bang a thupi ahong pai a; Pathian alalna ah athupi hi.
english: Out of the north comes golden splendor. With God is awesome majesty.

paite: Bangkim hihthei thu ahihleh, mu thei kei hang; thilhihtheihna ah athupi petmah hi. Huan vaihawmna leh dikna hauhna ah gim athuaksak kei ding hi.
english: We can’t reach the Almighty. He is exalted in power. In justice and great righteousness, he will not oppress.

paite: Huaiziak in mite'n amah alau ua; lungtang a pil kuamah alimsak kei hi."
english: Therefore men revere him. He doesn’t regard any who are wise of heart.”

paite: Huchi in TOUPA'N pingpei a kipan in Job adawng a, hichi in achi:
english: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,

paite: "Theihna bei thute a thuhilh hihmial hiai kua ahia?
english: “Who is this who darkens counsel by words without knowledge?

paite: Kipasalsak in tu in na kawng gak inla; hon dong ding ka hi, ka kiang a na gen ding ahi.
english: Brace yourself like a man, for I will question you, then you answer me!

paite: Lei kingaknate ka koih lai in nang koi ah na om a? Gen in, theihsiamna nei na hihleh.
english: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Declare, if you have understanding.

paite: Atehnate kua bawl ahia? Thei na hihleh! Atung a tehna khau kua zan ahia?
english: Who determined its measures, if you know? Or who stretched the line on it?

paite: Anuai suangphumte kua phum ahia? Huai aning a suang kua koih ahia?
english: Whereupon were its foundations fastened? Or who laid its cornerstone,

paite: Zingsang aksite'n la asakkhawm ua, Pathian tapate tengteng kipak a akikou lai un?
english: when the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?

paite: "Ahihkeileh kua'n kongkhakte in tuipite akhakbing a? Gil a kipan hong pawtkhia bang a, ahong puahkhiak lai in.
english: “Or who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke forth from the womb,

paite: Huai a puansilh meipi leh, khomial bikbek, huai a ding a tuamna puan ka bawl a,
english: when I made clouds its garment, and wrapped it in thick darkness,

paite: huai a ding a ka thupiak bawl a, kalhnate leh kongkhakte koih a,
english: marked out for it my bound, set bars and doors,

paite: hiai tan na hong pai ding, himahleh aban hilou in, ka chih a; hiai lai ah aki-uangsak na tuikihotte kholsak in a-om ding uh, ka chih lai in?
english: and said, ‘Here you may come, but no further. Here your proud waves shall be stayed?’

paite: Na nite akipat nungsiah zingsang thu na pia in, phalvak amun thei ding in na bawlta hia?
english: “Have you commanded the morning in your days, and caused the dawn to know its place;

paite: Lei tawpnate amat theih a, huai a kipan a gilou sinkhiak ahihtheihna ding in?
english: that it might take hold of the ends of the earth, and shake the wicked out of it?

paite: Chiamtehna nuai a tungman lei bang in mel akikheng a; puansilh bang in thil tengteng zenei in adingkhia hi.
english: It is changed as clay under the seal, and stands forth as a garment.

paite: Gilou a kipan a akhovak uh lettangsak ahi a, aban liksang uh akitan hi.
english: From the wicked, their light is withheld. The high arm is broken.

paite: "Tuipi nak sung ah na lutta hia? Ahihkeileh tui thuk tawp ah na paita hia?
english: “Have you entered into the springs of the sea? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?

paite: Sihna kongpite na kiang ah taklat in a-omta hia? Ahihkeileh sihna limliap kongpite na muta hia?
english: Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Or have you seen the gates of the shadow of death?

paite: Leitung zatdan na theisiamta hia? Puangkhia in, huai na theihleh.
english: Have you comprehended the earth in its breadth? Declare, if you know it all.

paite: Khovak tenna zotna lampi koi ah a-om a, huan khomial omna mun koisan ahia?
english: “What is the way to the dwelling of light? As for darkness, where is its place,

paite: Huchi a gamgi tan a na tonpih theih a, huai a inn tan a lampite na theihna ding in?
english: that you should take it to its bound, that you should discern the paths to its house?

paite: Thei mah niteh maw, huai lai a piangta hi ding hi chin a? Na nite atam mahmah ngal a!
english: Surely you know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!

paite: "Vuk koihkhawmna ah na lut ngei hia, ahihkeileh gial koihkhawmna na muta hia?
english: Have you entered the treasuries of the snow, or have you seen the treasures of the hail,

paite: Huai buaina hun a ding leh kidou leh kisat ni a dia ka koihkholhte?
english: which I have reserved against the time of trouble, against the day of battle and war?

paite: Bang lampi ah ahia khovak akikhen hiam leitung a suahlam huih adalhzak?
english: By what way is the lightning distributed, or the east wind scattered on the earth?

paite: Kua'n ahia tui tampi luanna ding a tuilam khuak a, kekkia a dia lampi sial?
english: Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunderstorm;

paite: Mihing omlouhna mun gam tung a vuah zusak ding in; mihing omlouhna, gamdai tung ah.
english: To cause it to rain on a land where no man is; on the wilderness, in which there is no man;

paite: Lei kisia leh segawpsa lungkimsak ding; loupa hing nou khangkhesak ding?
english: to satisfy the waste and desolate ground, to cause the tender grass to spring forth?

paite: Vuah in pa anei hia? Ahihkeileh daitui takte kua suan ahia?
english: Does the rain have a father? Or who fathers the drops of dew?

paite: Kua gil a kipan a tui khal hong pai ahia? Van daitui khal ngou, kua suahsak ahia?
english: Out of whose womb came the ice? The gray frost of the sky, who has given birth to it?

paite: Suang bang in tuite atak a, tui thuk maite akhal hi.
english: The waters become hard like stone, when the surface of the deep is frozen.

paite: "Siguk khaute na khihkhawm thei hia? zuheisuktun khaute na phel thei hia?
english: “Can you bind the cluster of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?

paite: Ama hunbi ah Aksi lamvak a chiamtehnate na pikhe thei hia? Ahihleh Zaangkhua leh tate na pi thei hia?
english: Can you lead forth the constellations in their season? Or can you guide the Bear with her cubs?

paite: Van thupiakte na thei hia? Huai lalna lei ah na dingkhesak thei diam?
english: Do you know the laws of the heavens? Can you establish its dominion over the earth?

paite: Nang tui tampi in akhuhtheihna ding in meipi kiang ah aw na suah thei diam?
english: “Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, That abundance of waters may cover you?

paite: Amau kiang ah, 'Hiai ah om ung,' chi a apaikhiak theihna ding un khophiate na sawlkhe thei a hia?
english: Can you send forth lightnings, that they may go? Do they report to you, ‘Here we are?’

paite: Sunggil lam ah pilna kua'n akoih a? Ahihkeileh lungsim kiang ah kua'n theihsiamna apia a?
english: Who has put wisdom in the inward parts? Or who has given understanding to the mind?

paite: Pilna in kua'n meipite asim thei dia? Van tuithawlte kua'n abokhe thei dia?
english: Who can number the clouds by wisdom? Or who can pour out the bottles of the sky,

paite: Alompi a leivui aluan a, asakte akimatkhawm ngiungeu lai un?
english: when the dust runs into a mass, and the clods of earth stick together?

paite: "Humpinelkai a ding in samat na betsak ding hia? Ahihkeileh humpinelkai noute gilkial na hihdam ding hia?
english: “Can you hunt the prey for the lioness, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,

paite: Akua ua aboh ua, buk ding a abukna mun ua a-om nilouh lai un?
english: when they crouch in their dens, and lie in wait in the thicket?

paite: Va-ak a ding a an kua'n pia ahia? Anoute Pathian kiang akikou a an duh man a avakvak lai un?"
english: Who provides for the raven his prey, when his young ones cry to God, and wander for lack of food?

paite: "Suangpi a gam sathakte'n nou asuaksak hun uh na thei hia? Ahihkeileh nou aneih lai uh na chiamteh thei hia?
english: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?

paite: Akha chinsak zah uh na thei hia? Ahihkeileh apian hun na thei hia?
english: Can you number the months that they fulfill? Or do you know the time when they give birth?

paite: Akun ua, atate uh asuang uh, alungkhamnate uh apaikhia uhi.
english: They bow themselves, they bring forth their young, they end their labor pains.

paite: Atate uh deihhuaitak in a-om ua, gamlak ah akhanglian ua; akuankhia ua, ahong kik nawn kei uh.
english: Their young ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They go forth, and don’t return again.

paite: "Kua'n gam sabiltung akhahkhia a? Ahihkeileh kua'n gam sabiltunghonte aphel a?
english: “Who has set the wild donkey free? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,

paite: Kua ahia a-inn ding a gamdai ka piak a, atenna ding a gamkeu ka bawlsak?
english: Whose home I have made the wilderness, and the salt land his dwelling place?

paite: Khopi buai nuanua amusit a, hawltute kikounate aza kei hi.
english: He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.

paite: Mual dungte agantatna mun ahi a, huan thil hing chiteng azong hi.
english: The range of the mountains is his pasture, He searches after every green thing.

paite: "Na nna sem ding in gam bawngtal alungkim hia? Ahihkeileh na anpiakna kiang ah a-om gige diam?
english: “Will the wild ox be content to serve you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?

paite: Leilehna ah khau in gam bawngtal na khihthei diam? Ahihkeileh na nung ah phaizangte atoktam diam?
english: Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys after you?

paite: Ahatna athupi ziak in, amah na muang diam? Ahihkeileh akiang ah na sepgimna na khiak diam?
english: Will you trust him, because his strength is great? Or will you leave to him your labor?

paite: Na buhchi inn ahon tut a, na buhphual a buh akaihkhawm theihna ding in amah na muang diam?
english: Will you confide in him, that he will bring home your seed, and gather the grain of your threshing floor?

paite: "Ostrik kha kisatheitak in akizap a; akhavengte leh amulte amigi hia?
english: “The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; but are they the feathers and plumage of love?

paite: Atuite lah leitung ah anusia a, leivui ah alumsak a,
english: For she leaves her eggs on the earth, warms them in the dust,

paite: Khe in asikkham thei chih a mangngilh a, ahihkeileh gamsa in asikgawp thei, chih.
english: and forgets that the foot may crush them, or that the wild animal may trample them.

paite: Amah a hilou bang in, anoute siatna ding in akhauh a; asepgimna bangmah lou himahleh, alau kei hi.
english: She deals harshly with her young ones, as if they were not hers. Though her labor is in vain, she is without fear,

paite: Pathian in pilna angolhsak ziak in, theihsiamna leng ape sam kei hi.
english: because God has deprived her of wisdom, neither has he imparted to her understanding.

paite: Tungsang lam a akitawisang chiang in, sakol leh atungtuangmi anuihsan.
english: When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.

paite: "Sakol hatna nang piak hia? Mul nem in angawng na tuam hia?
english: “Have you given the horse might? Have you clothed his neck with a quivering mane?

paite: Khaukhup bang in na tawmsak hia? Ahamna thupi alauhuai ve.
english: Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.

paite: Guam ah lei akhuat a, ahatna ah akipak a, mi kigalthuamte tuak ding in apaikhia.
english: He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his strength. He goes out to meet the armed men.

paite: Lauhuai anuihsan a, alungdong kei a, namsau leng anungngat sam kei hi.
english: He mocks at fear, and is not dismayed, neither does he turn back from the sword.

paite: Amah ah thalbawm aging lengleng a, teipite zelzel leh chiangzum.
english: The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.

paite: Kihtakhuaina leh hehna in lei anawmvalh a; Pengkul aw ahi chih leng agingta sam kei hi.
english: He eats up the ground with fierceness and rage, neither does he stand still at the sound of the trumpet.

paite: Pengkul agin teng in, 'Hah' achi a, kidouna, heutute vanpiging leh kikou, gamlapi a pan athei.
english: As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!’ He smells the battle afar off, the thunder of the captains, and the shouting.

paite: "Na pilna in mu sangpi a lengsak in, akhate simlam ah aphalh hia?
english: “Is it by your wisdom that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the south?

paite: Nang thupiak in hia muvanlai in tungsang a leng a abu aseh?
english: Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?

paite: Suangpi tung ah ateng a, huai ah giahna anei a, suanghengte leh kulh muanhuaite ah.
english: On the cliff he dwells, and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.

paite: Huai a kipan in mat ding amu a; amitte'n gamla amu hi.
english: From there he spies out the prey. His eyes see it afar off.

paite: Anoute'n leng sisan atawpbei ua; thah a a-omna mun, huai ah a-om hi.”
english: His young ones also suck up blood. Where the slain are, there he is.”

paite: Huai lai in Eliphaz, Teman mi in adawng a hichi in achi:
"Mi'n nang hon houlimpih tumleh na zadah diam? Himahleh pau lou in kua a-om thei dia?
english: “If someone ventures to talk with you, will you be grieved? But who can withhold himself from speaking?

paite: Ngai in, mi tampi na hilhta a, khut hatloute na hihhatta hi.
english: Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the weak hands.

paite: Apuk lai in na thute'n adingsak a, khuk hatloute na kipsak hi.
english: Your words have supported him who was falling, You have made firm the feeble knees.

paite: Himahleh tu in na tung ah ahong tung a, na bah a; nang ahon khoih a, na buaita hi.
english: But now it has come to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.

paite: Pathian na kihtakna, na muanna hilou hia, na lametna na lampite muanhuaina?
english: Isn’t your piety your confidence? Isn’t the integrity of your ways your hope?

paite: Theigige in, ka hon ngen ahi, hoih hinapi a, mangthang ngei kua ahia? Ahihkeileh koi lai ah ahia midik satkhiak a a-om?
english: “Remember, now, whoever perished, being innocent? Or where were the upright cut off?

paite: Kei muh in, thulimlouhna lei lette ahi ua, buaina tuh a huai mah atte.
english: According to what I have seen, those who plow iniquity, and sow trouble, reap the same.

paite: Pathian hu in amangthang ua, hehna a mut a hihmang in a-om uhi.
english: By the breath of God they perish. By the blast of his anger are they consumed.

paite: Humpinelkai humham leh, humpinelkai hangsan aw leh, humpinelkai tuailai hate, akitanta hi.
english: The roaring of the lion, and the voice of the fierce lion, the teeth of the young lions, are broken.

paite: Samat taksap ziak in humpinelkai tek amangthang a, huan humpinelkaipi noute adalhzak uhi.
english: The old lion perishes for lack of prey. The cubs of the lioness are scattered abroad.

paite: "Tu in aguk in thil ka kiang a hong tung ka bil in huai a huauna asangta hi.
english: “Now a thing was secretly brought to me. My ear received a whisper of it.

paite: Zan mengmuhna a kipan angaihtuahnate ah, mite nakpitak a a-ihmut san lai un,
english: In thoughts from the visions of the night, when deep sleep falls on men,

paite: ka tung ah launa ahong tung a, linna in ka guhte tengteng asing hi.
english: fear came on me, and trembling, which made all my bones shake.

paite: Huai lai in ka mai ah kha apai a; ka chimul adinghta hi.
english: Then a spirit passed before my face. The hair of my flesh stood up.

paite: Ka dingh kinken a, himahleh huai a kilatdan ka theikak theita kei a; alim tuh ka mit ma ah a-om a; daihna a-om a, aw ka za hi,
english: It stood still, but I couldn’t discern its appearance. A form was before my eyes. Silence, then I heard a voice, saying,

paite: Pathian sang in sithei mihing dikzaw ding hia? Abawlpa sang in mihing siangthouzaw ding hia? chi in.
english: ‘Shall mortal man be more just than God? Shall a man be more pure than his Maker?

paite: Ngai in, asikhate ah muanna akoih kei a; angelte hai in angoh hi:
english: Behold, he puts no trust in his servants. He charges his angels with error.

paite: Tungman inn a teng amaute hi sem na un chia, asuangphum leivui a om a, leikha ma a chimsia.
english: How much more, those who dwell in houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust, who are crushed before the moth!

paite: Zingsang leh nitak kikal in hihsiat in a-om ua; theih louh hial in tangtawn in amangthang uhi.
english: Between morning and evening they are destroyed. They perish forever without any regarding it.

paite: Amau sung a apuanin khau uh bohkhiak touh hilou hia? Pilna tel lou in asi uhi."
english: Isn’t their tent cord plucked up within them? They die, and that without wisdom.’

paite: Huai lou in TOUPA'N Job adawng a, hichi in achi:
"Kuapeuh awlmoh nei lou in thil Bangkim hihthei akiselpih diam? Kuapeuh Pathian kiselpih, huai tuh amah dawngsak un."
english: “Shall he who argues contend with the Almighty? He who argues with God, let him answer it.”

paite: Job in TOUPA adawng a, hichi in achi:
"Ngai in, bangmah ka hita kei a; bangchi in ka hon dawng dia? Ka kam ah ka khut ka koih.
english: “Behold, I am of small account. What shall I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.

paite: Khatvei ka pauta a, ka dawng kei ding; ahi, nihvei himahleh ka pau nawn kei ding.”
english: I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.”

paite: Toupa'n pingpei a kipan in Job adawng a, hichi in achi.
english: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,

paite: "Kipasalsak inla, tu in na kawng gak in. Nang a kipan ka hon phut dia, kei kiang ah na hon puang ding hi.
english: “Now brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer me.

paite: Ka vaihawmna bangmah lou a koih ding na hiam? Siam na tantheihna dia, kei hon mohpaih ding na hi hia?
english: Will you even annul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?

paite: Ahihkeileh Pathian bang in ban na nei hia? Amah bang in aw in vanpi na gingsak thei hia?
english: Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?

paite: Tu in nang hoihkim leh zahna in kizem in; zahna leh lalna in kivan in.
english: “Now deck yourself with excellency and dignity. Array yourself with honor and majesty.

paite: Na hehna dimlette sungkhia in; michih kisatheite en inla, hihniam in.
english: Pour out the fury of your anger. Look at everyone who is proud, and bring him low.

paite: Michih kisathei en inla, kainiam in; adinna uah migiloute tuanchil in.
english: Look at everyone who is proud, and humble him. Crush the wicked in their place.

paite: Leivui ah amaute selkhawm in; mundai ah amai uh kan in.
english: Hide them in the dust together. Bind their faces in the hidden place.

paite: Huchi in na khut taklam in nang ahondam thei chih ka hon thei ding.
english: Then I will also admit to you that your own right hand can save you.

paite: "Ngai dih, nang ka hon siam bang a ka siam, tu in behemoth en in; bawngtal bang in loupa ane hi.
english: “See now, behemoth, which I made as well as you. He eats grass as an ox.

paite: En in tu in, akawng ah ahatna a-om a, agilpi thate ah ahatna a-om hi
english: Look now, his strength is in his thighs. His force is in the muscles of his belly.

paite: Sidar sing bang in amei atangsak a, apheite thaguite phankhawm in a-om hi.
english: He moves his tail like a cedar. The sinews of his thighs are knit together.

paite: Aguhte dal lawng ahi a, aguh leh tangte siktawn bang ahi.
english: His bones are like tubes of brass. His limbs are like bars of iron.

paite: "Pathian lampite amakai lianpen ahi, amah bawlpa kia in anamsau amah kiang lam naih ding in abawl thei ding.
english: He is the chief of the ways of God. He who made him gives him his sword.

paite: Chihtaktak in mualte'n amah an apuak ua; gamsate tengteng mawlna mun ah.
english: Surely the mountains produce food for him, where all the animals of the field play.

paite: Singbawk limte nuai ah alum a, pumpeng kawm leh chiknawng lak ah.
english: He lies under the lotus trees, in the covert of the reed, and the marsh.

paite: Tui lili singte'n alim un akhuh ua; lui gei singnah kaite'n atuam kimvel uhi.
english: The lotuses cover him with their shade. The willows of the brook surround him.

paite: Ngai in, lui adimletleh, aling kei a; akam chiang pha hial in Jordan khang mahleh, amuang hi.
english: Behold, if a river overflows, he doesn’t tremble. He is confident, though the Jordan swells even to his mouth.

paite: Akiven lai in kuapeuh in amah sikkawi in aman diam, thang in anak avut pailet diam?”
english: Shall any take him when he is on the watch, or pierce through his nose with a snare?

paite: “Ngakuai in Leviathan na kaikhe thei diam? Ahihkeileh akhau in alei na sawntum thei diam?
english: “Can you draw out Leviathan Leviathan is a name for a crocodile or similar creature. with a fishhook, or press down his tongue with a cord?

paite: Anak sung ah khauhual na thun thei diam? Ahihkeileh sikkawi in ahaizek na vut pailet thei diam?
english: Can you put a rope into his nose, or pierce his jaw through with a hook?

paite: Na kiang ah thilnget tampi abawl diam? Ahihkeileh na kiang ah thu nemte agen diam?
english: Will he make many petitions to you, or will he speak soft words to you?

paite: Tangtawn a ding in amah sikha dia na laktheihna ding in, nang toh thukhun abawl diam?
english: Will he make a covenant with you, that you should take him for a servant forever?

paite: Vasa toh bang in amah toh na mawl diam? Ahihkeileh na sikhanute a ding in amah na hen diam?
english: Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you bind him for your girls?

paite: Ngaman mite'n amah sumsinna ding in abawl ding uam? Sumsin mite lak ah amah azuak ding uam?
english: Will traders barter for him? Will they part him among the merchants?

paite: Siklen in avun na dimsak thei diam, ahihkeileh alu ngalingte in?
english: Can you fill his skin with barbed irons, or his head with fish spears?

paite: Atung ah na khut koih in; kidouna theigige in, huchi in na hih nawn kei ding hi.
english: Lay your hand on him. Remember the battle, and do so no more.

paite: "Ngai in, amah lametna bangmah lou ahi; amah muh mahmah in mi paihkhiak in a-om kei dia hia?
english: Behold, the hope of him is in vain. Won’t one be cast down even at the sight of him?

paite: Amah hihhalh ngam khop ding in kuamah ahang kei; ka ma a dingh kua ahia le?
english: None is so fierce that he dare stir him up. Who then is he who can stand before me?

paite: Amah ka dit ding, ka kiang ah kua'n ape masa a le? Van nuai a om peuhmah kei' a ahi.
english: Who has first given to me, that I should repay him? Everything under the heavens is mine.

paite: "Aguh-le-tang thu ah ka dai kei ding, ahatna mahmah leh, apum kilawmna ah leng.
english: “I will not keep silence concerning his limbs, nor his mighty strength, nor his goodly frame.

paite: Apuansilh tungnung kua'n asuahsak thei dia? Akamkaih thuah nih sung ah kua ahong pai dia?
english: Who can strip off his outer garment? Who shall come within his jaws?

paite: Amai kongkhakte kua'n ahong thei dia? Aha kimvel ah lauhuaina a-om.
english: Who can open the doors of his face? Around his teeth is terror.

paite: Alip hattakte akisaktheihna ahi, namkipsa bang a khakkhum ahi.
english: Strong scales are his pride, shut up together with a close seal.

paite: Akal ua huihzam alut theihlouhna ding in, khat in adang anaih mahmah.
english: One is so near to another, that no air can come between them.

paite: Khat leh adang akizom ua, akisoumat ua, khen theih louh in a-om uh.
english: They are joined one to another. They stick together, so that they can’t be pulled apart.

paite: Ahahchhiaite'n avaksak a, amitte zingsang mitvunte bang ahi.
english: His sneezing flashes out light. His eyes are like the eyelids of the morning.

paite: Akam a pan meikuangte apawtkhia, mei-ekte atawmkhia hi.
english: Out of his mouth go burning torches. Sparks of fire leap forth.

paite: Anakvangte a kipan in meikhu apawt a, halsianna bel leh chiklak loupa kang a kipan bang in.
english: Out of his nostrils a smoke goes, as of a boiling pot over a fire of reeds.

paite: "Ahu in suang akuangsak a, akam a pan meikuang apawtkhia hi.
english: His breath kindles coals. A flame goes forth from his mouth.

paite: Angawng ah hatna a-om gige a, ama ah lauhuaina alam hi.
english: There is strength in his neck. Terror dances before him.

paite: Asa thate akizomkhawm ua, atung ah akip ua; hihtat theih in a-om kei uh.
english: The flakes of his flesh are joined together. They are firm on him. They can’t be moved.

paite: Alungtang suang bang in akip a; ahi, buhgawina suang nuainung bang ahi.
english: His heart is as firm as a stone, yes, firm as the lower millstone.

paite: Amah athoh chiang in, mihatte alau uh; lauh luatna ziak in omdan ding athei kei uh.
english: When he raises himself up, the mighty are afraid. They retreat before his thrashing.

paite: Mi'n amah namsau in satleh, aphatuam kei hi; teipi hiam, thal hiam, sikmuk zum hiam in leng.
english: If one attacks him with the sword, it can’t prevail; nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.

paite: Buhpawl bang in sik asim a, sing muatsa bang in dalsik.
english: He counts iron as straw; and brass as rotten wood.

paite: Thal in amah ataisak thei kei ding; amah lak ah vaisuanglot suangte buhpawl asuak hi.
english: The arrow can’t make him flee. Sling stones are like chaff to him.

paite: "Khetbukte buhpawl bang a sim ahi. Teipi ging anuihsan hi.
english: Clubs are counted as stubble. He laughs at the rushing of the javelin.

paite: Anuailam pangte belpei ahi, buannawi tung ah buhkhetna chiang bang in akiphah hi.
english: His undersides are like sharp potsherds, leaving a trail in the mud like a threshing sledge.

paite: Tui thukte belpi sou bolhbolh ding in abawl a, tuipi nuh theih bawm in abawl hi.
english: He makes the deep to boil like a pot. He makes the sea like a pot of ointment.

paite: Anung ah lampi avaksak a; tui thuk samkang nei asa uhi.
english: He makes a path shine after him. One would think the deep had white hair.

paite: Leitung ah amah bang a lauh nei lou a-om kei a,
english: On earth there is not his equal, that is made without fear.

paite: Thil sang chiteng a-en a, kisathei tapate tengteng tung ah kumpipa ahi."
english: He sees everything that is high. He is king over all the sons of pride.”

paite: Huchi in Job in TOUPA dawng hichi in achi.
"Thil bangkim na hihthei chih leh nang thiltup kham theih ahi kei chih ka thei hi.
english: “I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.

paite: Hiai thuhilhna theihna tel lou a sel kua ahia? Huaiziak in ka theihsiam louh, ka theih louh, kei a dia thillamdang luate ka genkhia hi.
english: You asked, ‘Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?’ therefore I have uttered that which I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, which I didn’t know.

paite: "Za in, ka hon ngen ahi, ka pau ding; nang ka hon phut ding, kei lam ah nang puang in, na hon chi hi.
english: You said, ‘Listen, now, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will answer me.’

paite: Zakna bil in nang ka hon za a; himahleh tu in ka mit in ka hon mu a,
english: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.

paite: Huaiziak in ka kikih a, leivui leh meivu ah ka kisik hi."
english: Therefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, huchi a TOUPA'N Job kiang a hiai thute agen khit in, TOUPA'N Teman mi Eliphaz kiang ah, "Ka hehna nang tung leh na lawm nihte tung ah akuang, ka sikha Job bang a noute'n ka tanchin thil dik na gen louh ziak un," achi hi.
english: It was so, that after Yahweh had spoken these words to Job, Yahweh said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is kindled against you, and against your two friends; for you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.

paite: "Huaiziak in tu in, bawngtal sagih leh belamtal sagih la unla, ka sikha Job kiang ah hoh unla, nou a ding in halmang thillat lan un; huchi in noute a ding in ka sikha Job athum ding a; amah vang in ka sang dia, huchi in na haina uh dungzui in na tung uah ka hih kei ding; ka sikha Job bang in lah ka tanchin thil dik na gen kei uh," chi in.
english: Now therefore, take to yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you, for I will accept him, that I not deal with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job has.”

paite: Huchi in Teman mi Eliphaz leh Shuah mi Bildad leh Naamath mi Zophar akuan ua, TOUPA'N thu apiak bang in ahihta uhi. TOUPA'N Job asangta hi.
english: So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did what Yahweh commanded them, and Yahweh accepted Job.

paite: Alawmte a dia Job athum zoh in TOUPA'N Job saltanna akiheisak a, TOUPA'N Job ama a aneih zahnih apeta hi.
english: Yahweh turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends. Yahweh gave Job twice as much as he had before.

paite: Huai lai in akiang ah, a-unaute tengteng leh asanggamnute tengteng leh tuma lam a amel theihsa tengteng leh a-insung a tanghou amah toh nete ahong pai ua, amah anem ua, TOUPA'N atung a hoih lou atunsak tengteng tungtang thu ah amah alungmuan uhi. Michih in leng ama sum leh michih in dangka-eng bilbah apia uhi.
english: Then came there to him all his brothers, and all his sisters, and all those who had been of his acquaintance before, and ate bread with him in his house. They comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the evil that Yahweh had brought on him. Everyone also gave him a piece of money, literally, kesitah, a unit of money, probably silver and everyone a ring of gold.

paite: Huchi in TOUPA'N Job tawpna lam a kipatna lam sang in anak vualzawl zaw hi. Belam singkhat-le-sangli leh sangawngsau sangguk leh bawngtal sangkhat leh sabengtungnu sangkhat anei hi.
english: So Yahweh blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand female donkeys.

paite: Tapa sagih leh tanu thum leng anei hi.
english: He had also seven sons and three daughters.

paite: Amasapen, Jemima achi a; anihna min, Kezia; athumna min, Keren-happuk.
english: He called the name of the first, Jemimah; and the name of the second, Keziah; and the name of the third, Keren Happuch.

paite: Huchi in gamsung pumpi ah Job tanute bang a melhoih a-om kei uh; apa un a-unaute lak ah goutan amaute apia hi.
english: In all the land were no women found so beautiful as the daughters of Job. Their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.

paite: Huai nung in Job, kum za-le-sawmli adam a, atapate leh atapate' tapate, khang lina tan amu hi.
english: After this Job lived one hundred forty years, and saw his sons, and his sons’ sons, to four generations.

paite: Huchi in Job atek mahmah a, a-upat tak ziak in asita hi.
english: So Job died, being old and full of days.

paite: "Tu in sam in; nang hon dawng kua a-om a? Misiangthoute lak ah akua lam na nga dia?
english: “Call now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

paite: Lungzinna in lah mihai athat a, huan thikna in mimawl athat sek hi.
english: For resentment kills the foolish man, and jealousy kills the simple.

paite: Mihai zungkai ka muta a; himahleh thakhat in atenna aka hamsiat hi.
english: I have seen the foolish taking root, but suddenly I cursed his habitation.

paite: Bitna a kipan gamlapi ah atate a-om ua, kongpi ah hihgawp in a-om uh, kuamah amaute hunkhe ding a-om kei uhi.
english: His children are far from safety. They are crushed in the gate. Neither is there any to deliver them,

paite: Agilkial in ling lak a kipan nangawn a-an kaihkhawm agaihsak a, suamhat in aneih-le-lam anawmvalhsak hi.
english: whose harvest the hungry eats up, and take it even out of the thorns. The snare gapes for their substance.

paite: Gimthuakna leivui a kipan in ahong pawt kei a, lei a kipan in buaina leng ahong dawnkhe sam kei hi.
english: For affliction doesn’t come forth from the dust, neither does trouble spring out of the ground;

paite: Himahleh mihing buai ding mah apiang ahi, mei-ekte atoulen bang in.
english: but man is born to trouble, as the sparks fly upward.

paite: "Himahleh ke'n ahihleh, Pathian lam ah ka zong ding a, Pathian kiang ah ka thu ka koih ding hi.
english: “But as for me, I would seek God. I would commit my cause to God,

paite: Thil thupite hihpa leh zonkhiak theih louh; sim zoh louh thillamdangte,
english: who does great things that can’t be fathomed, marvelous things without number;

paite: leitung a vuah pepa leh, loute tung a tui sawlpa.
english: who gives rain on the earth, and sends waters on the fields;

paite: Huchi in ama'n aniamsate tungsang ah akoihtou a; misi suunte muanna ah atawisang hi.
english: so that he sets up on high those who are low, those who mourn are exalted to safety.

paite: Zekhem hatte lunggelte bangmah lou asuaksak a, huchi in akhutte un athiltup uh ahihthei kei uhi.
english: He frustrates the devices of the crafty, So that their hands can’t perform their enterprise.

paite: Mipilte akhemhatna un aman a, mihoihloute thilgel athalpaihsak hi.
english: He takes the wise in their own craftiness; the counsel of the cunning is carried headlong.

paite: Sun lai in khomialna athuak ua, zan lai bang in suntang lai in amai maimah uhi.
english: They meet with darkness in the day time, and grope at noonday as in the night.

paite: Himahleh ama'n gentheite mihatte kam leh khut a kipan leh tasamte mahmah namsau a kipan ahondam hi.
english: But he saves from the sword of their mouth, even the needy from the hand of the mighty.

paite: Huchi in mizawng in lametna anei а, thulimlouhna in akam ahumsak hi.
english: So the poor has hope, and injustice shuts her mouth.

paite: "Ngai in, Pathian in abawlhoih mi in nuam asa hi; huaiziak in Bangkim hihthei sawina musit ke'n.
english: “Behold, happy is the man whom God corrects. Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.

paite: Ama'n lah meima abawl a, atuam a, aliamsak a, akhut in adamsak hi.
english: For he wounds, and binds up. He injures, and his hands make whole.

paite: Buaina guk ah ahon suaktasak ding a; ahi, sagih ah gilou in nang ahon khoih kei ding hi.
english: He will deliver you in six troubles; yes, in seven no evil shall touch you.

paite: Kial chiang in nang sihna a kipan ahon tan ding; namsau thilhihtheihna a kipan, kidou chiang in.
english: In famine he will redeem you from death; in war, from the power of the sword.

paite: Kam sung a leizepna a kipan ahon sel ding a; siatna ahong tun chiang in na lau sam kei ding hi.
english: You shall be hidden from the scourge of the tongue, neither shall you be afraid of destruction when it comes.

paite: Siatna leh kialna ah na nui ding a, lei gamsate na kihta kei ding hi.
english: At destruction and famine you shall laugh, neither shall you be afraid of the animals of the earth.

paite: Gam a suangte toh na kithuahtheih ding ziak un; huan gam a gamsate nang toh na kituak ding uhi.
english: For you shall be allied with the stones of the field. The animals of the field shall be at peace with you.

paite: "Na puanin muang in a-om chih na thei ding a; na ganhuang na veh ding a, bangmah kim lou a-om kei ding hi.
english: You shall know that your tent is in peace. You shall visit your fold, and shall miss nothing.

paite: Na chite leng athupi ding a, na suante lei a loupa bang in a-om ding uh chih na thei ding hi.
english: You shall know also that your seed shall be great, Your offspring as the grass of the earth.

paite: Kum ching in na hankhuk na zuan ding a, ahun a buhlak a-om bang in.
english: You shall come to your grave in a full age, like a shock of grain comes in its season.

paite: Ngai in, hiai thu i zongta ua, adik mah ahi, za in na hoihna ding in thei in."
english: Look this, we have searched it, so it is. Hear it, and know it for your good.”

paite: Huchi in Job in adawng a, hichi in achi:
"Aw ka lungzinna kibuk thei hi henla, ka tuahsiatna selbukna ah kikoihkhawm thei hileh!
english: “Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my calamity laid in the balances!

paite: Tu in tuipite a piaunel sang in agikzaw ding: huaiziak in ka thugente leng akhauh hi.
english: For now it would be heavier than the sand of the seas, therefore have my words been rash.

paite: Bangkim hihthei thalte lah ka sung ah a-om ngal a, agu uh huai a kipan a ka kha in adawnvek; kei dou ding in Pathian mulkimhuainate akivual uhi.
english: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me. My spirit drinks up their poison. The terrors of God set themselves in array against me.

paite: "Anek ding loupa mu, gam sabiltung aham a hia? Ahihkeileh gan an mu bawngtal aham a hia?
english: Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?

paite: Chi tel lou in gim nei lou akine thei dia hia? Ahihkeileh aktuida ah limna mawngmawng a-om a hia?
english: Can that which has no flavor be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?

paite: Ka kha in amaute akhoih nuam kei; kei a ding in an kihhuai bang ahi uhi.
english: My soul refuses to touch them. They are as loathsome food to me.

paite: "Aw ka nget tang thei leng zaw; ka thil deih Pathian in hon phalleh zaw.
english: “Oh that I might have my request, that God would grant the thing that I long for,

paite: Kei hon hihgawp ding in Pathian deihlam hi lai henla; akhut zan in, kei hon satkhe maileh.
english: even that it would please God to crush me; that he would let loose his hand, and cut me off!

paite: Huchi in lungmuanna ka nei lai dia; ahi, damlou natna ah ka kipak ding hi; Mi Siangthou thute ka kitheihmohbawl ngal kei a.
english: Be it still my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn’t spare, that I have not denied the words of the Holy One.

paite: Ka hatna bang ahia, ka ngak ding? Huan ka beina bang ahia, ka kuhkal ding?
english: What is my strength, that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?

paite: Ka hatna suangte hatna hi hia? Ahihkeileh ka sa dalsik hia?
english: Is my strength the strength of stones? Or is my flesh of brass?

paite: Kei ah panpihna a-om het kei a, kei a kipan theihsiamna hawlmang in.
english: Isn’t it that I have no help in me, That wisdom is driven quite from me?

paite: "Bah dia mansa a om kiang ah alawm in siamna a-etsak ding ahi kei maw; huchi lou in Bangkim hihthei kihtakna tawpsan ahi kei ding maw.
english: “To him who is ready to faint, kindness should be shown from his friend; even to him who forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

paite: Luita bang in ka unaute alepchiah uh; luita mangthang luanna bang in.
english: My brothers have dealt deceitfully as a brook, as the channel of brooks that pass away;

paite: Huai tui khal ziak a vom a; huai a vukkhal akisel.
english: Which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow hides itself.

paite: Alum hun chiang in atuimang ua, asat chiang in amun ua kipan amangthang uhi.
english: In the dry season, they vanish. When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.

paite: Huai lampi a khualzinte a pial ua, bangmah omlouhna mun ah apaitou ua, amangthang uh.
english: The caravans that travel beside them turn aside. They go up into the waste, and perish.

paite: Tema khualzinte'n azong ua, Sheba pawlte'n alamen uh.
english: The caravans of Tema looked. The companies of Sheba waited for them.

paite: Akilamet hang un azahlak uh; huai lam ah ava pai ua azahlak uh.
english: They were distressed because they were confident. They came there, and were confounded.

paite: Tu in bangmah na hi ngal kei ua; mulkimhuaina na mu ua, na lau uhi.
english: For now you are nothing. You see a terror, and are afraid.

paite: Kei hon pia un? Ahihkeileh na neih-le-lam ua kipan in kei a ding in thilpiak lan un, ka chi hia?
english: Did I say, ‘Give to me?’ or, ‘Offer a present for me from your substance?’

paite: Ahihkeileh, melma khut a pan hon tan un, mihat khut a pan hon hukhia un ka chi hia?
english: or, ‘Deliver me from the adversary’s hand?’ or, ‘Redeem me from the hand of the oppressors?’

paite: "Hon sinsak in, huan ka dai ding: ka diklouhna hon theisiamsak un.
english: “Teach me, and I will hold my peace. Cause me to understand wherein I have erred.

paite: Thudikna thute hat hi nah e: himahleh miselna in bang aselphou a?
english: How forcible are words of uprightness! But your reproof, what does it reprove?

paite: Thute selphou ding a um na hi uhia? Chimoh mi thugente huih bang ahi chih thei in.
english: Do you intend to reprove words, since the speeches of one who is desperate are as wind?

paite: Ahi, pa neiloute tung ah ai na san ua, na lawm uh sumsinna van in na bawl uh.
english: Yes, you would even cast lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your friend.

paite: Tu in hehpih in hon en un; na ma uah thuzuau ka gen kei a.
english: Now therefore be pleased to look at me, for surely I shall not lie to your face.

paite: Kik nawn un ka hon ngen ahi, diklouhna om kei hen; ahi, kik nawn un, ka thu adik ahi.
english: Please return. Let there be no injustice. Yes, return again. My cause is righteous.

paite: Ka lei ah diklouhna a-om hia? Ka lei in thil hoih lou atheikak thei kei dia hia?"
english: Is there injustice on my tongue? Can’t my taste discern mischievous things?

paite: "Leitung ah mihing a ding in kidouna a-om kei maw? Anite kilohmi nite bang ahi kei a hia?
english: “Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand?

paite: Limliap deih mahmah sikha bang in, aloh lamen kilohmi bang in.
english: As a servant who earnestly desires the shadow, as a hireling who looks for his wages,

paite: Huai bang in bangmah lou khate nei ding a bawl ka hi, huan kei a ding in zan chimhuaite seh ahi.
english: so am I made to possess months of misery, wearisome nights are appointed to me.

paite: Ka lup chiang in, chikchiang in ka thou dia? ka chi a; himahleh zan asawt hi; lehlam lehlam ah nisuah matan kilumlet in ka om hi.
english: When I lie down, I say, ‘When shall I arise, and the night be gone?’ I toss and turn until the dawning of the day.

paite: Ka sa than leh leivui khal in atuam a; ka vun kimat in apuakkham hi.
english: My flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust. My skin closes up, and breaks out afresh.

paite: Ka nite siamganmi khohthei sang in akinzaw a, lametna bei a zatbei ahi.
english: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle, and are spent without hope.

paite: "Aw ka hinna huih ahi chih theigige in; ka mit in hoih amu nawn kei ding hi.
